arguments.withSecret_data: rdi; pointer to the input bytes. Read on every modelled path (read64/read32/byte loads per branch), never written
arguments.withSecret_length: rsi; input length in bytes (size_t). Dispatched on at 0x61db965 (cmp $0x10) and 0x61db96b (cmp $0x8); the 4..8 branch reads data+len-4, the 9..16 branch reads data+len-8
arguments.withSecret_secret: rdx; pointer to the caller-supplied secret (at least 72 bytes are read on the short path: highest read is secret+64..72 in the len-0 branch). No minimum-size check is visible on the short path
arguments.withSecret_secretSize: rcx; the secret size. Not read on the len<=16 path; carried (rbp) into the >240 hashLong path only
arguments.withSeed_data: rdi; pointer to the input bytes, same reads as withSecret
arguments.withSeed_length: rsi; input length in bytes. Dispatched on at 0x61dc0c7 (cmp $0x10) and 0x61dc0cd (cmp $0x8)
arguments.withSeed_seed: rdx; 64-bit seed, saved to r8 at entry. Folded into the secret words (+ seed / - seed) per branch; the len-4..8 branch additionally applies the public seed transform seed ^= swap32(seed as u32) << 32

census.direct_calls_note: Whole-.text E8 scan found no direct call site targeting 0x61db940 or 0x61dc0c0, and no lea (48 8d /r rip-relative) or ff 25 jmp reference to either address. The binary's symbol table is stripped (the strings ROCKSDB_XXH3_64bits_withSecret / _withSeed do not occur in the file), so no exported-symbol entry can be cited either. Both functions are therefore recorded with no in-binary consumer contract; they are public C API entry points of the vendored xxHash and are reachable in principle from outside the node binary
census.sibling_callers: The default-secret one-shot ROCKSDB_XXH3_64bits at 0x61db650 is the callee of the ComputeBuiltinChecksumWithLastByte type-4 arm (0x616bd60); withSecret/withSeed are its secret/seed variants and share the short-branch core

model.len_0: XXH64_avalanche(seed ^ (secret[56:64] ^ secret[64:72])); withSecret uses seed 0, withSeed folds the default-secret xor into the immediate 0x8726f9105dc21ddc
model.len_1_to_3: combined = data[len-1] | data[0]<<16 | len<<8 | data[len>>1]<<24; bitflip = (read32(secret) ^ read32(secret+4)) + seed; XXH64_avalanche(combined ^ bitflip). withSeed folds the word xor into the immediate 0x87275a9b
model.len_4_to_8: seed ^= swap32(seed as u32) << 32; input64 = read32(data+len-4) + (read32(data) << 32); bitflip = (read64(secret+8) ^ read64(secret+16)) - seed; rrmxmx(input64 ^ bitflip, len). The seed transform and the input64 packing were confirmed against the published xxh3.h source (v0.7.3) after an early draft misread both; the binary matches the public formulas exactly
model.len_9_to_16: bitflip1 = (secret[24] ^ secret[32]) + seed; bitflip2 = (secret[40] ^ secret[48]) - seed; lo = read64(data) ^ bitflip1; hi = read64(data+len-8) ^ bitflip2; XXH3_avalanche(len + bswap64(lo) + hi + mul128_fold64(lo, hi)). withSeed folds the word xors into the immediates 0x6782737bea4239b9 (+ seed) and 0xaf56bc3b0996523a (- seed)

return_value: 64-bit hash in %rax. withSecret returns the hash for the caller secret; withSeed for the default secret keyed by the seed

semantics.scope: Lengths 0..16 only, both entry points. The 17..128, 129..240 and >240 branches are recorded in branches.tsv with their dispatch sites and delegation targets (len_17to128 inline, len_129to240 at 0x61d7dc0, hashLong_withSecret inline SIMD / hashLong_withSeed at 0x61d9090) and are out of scope for this packet
semantics.secretSize: withSecret never reads its 4th argument on the modelled path; a short secret would read out of bounds, but no check is visible in the body
semantics.seed_transform: Only the len-4..8 branch transforms the seed (swap32 of the low word into the high word, xored with the seed). All other short branches add or subtract the seed directly on the secret-word xors

side_effects: Neither function writes memory, calls out (except the stack-canary failure path to __stack_chk_fail), or reads outside [data, data+len) and the secret windows listed in the model. The stack canary is checked on the withSecret return paths (0x61db9c5, 0x61dc01f) and withSeed returns directly

tests.cases: 2,400 deterministic cases (1,200 per entry point; lengths 0..16 cycled; withSecret over the default secret plus 7 seeded-random 192-byte secrets; withSeed over 12 seeds including 0, 1, 2, PRIME64_1 and 0xffffffffffffffff). Transliteration vs independent public-formula reference: 0 mismatches. See result.json
tests.published_anchors: XXH3_64bits(b'', 0) = 0x2d06800538d394c2 and XXH3_64bits(b'a', 0) = 0xe6c632b61e964e1f hold through both entry points (default secret / seed 0)
tests.unit_tests: tests/test_xxh3_with_secret_seed115.py, 13 tests (published anchors, per-branch secret-window sensitivity, seed sensitivity, withSeed(data, 0) == withSecret(data, kSecret), out-of-scope length rejection, binary grounding, result regeneration)

unknowns: No in-binary caller for either function (see census): no consumer contract, no call-site seed or secret is known from the node

The 17..128 branch's last mix reads secret+16/secret+24 for the trailing 16 bytes; the packet does not claim a public-source identity for that branch (out of scope) and notes the offsets only as observed
Whether any Rust caller passes a non-default secret to withSecret, and what secretSize values are passed, is not established from the binary

The len_129to240 helper at 0x61d7dc0 and the hashLong_withSeed helper at 0x61d9090 are delegation targets only; their bodies are not reconstructed here (the withSeed long helper has a .constprop.0 census record; the len_129to240 helper is shared with the default-secret path)
